title: But was young Boasthard’s fear
html_source: This section (“But was young Boasthard’s fear” through “bring brenningly biddeth”) is in the style of John Bunyan’s allegorical novel Pilgrim’s Progress.

anchor.prefix: it was no other thing but a hubbub noise that he heard, the discharge of fluid from the thunderhead, look you, having taken place, and all of the order of a natural phenomenon.
anchor.suffix: vanquished by Calmer's words? No, for he had in his bosom a spike named Bitterness which could not by words be done away. And was he then neither calm like the one nor godly like
